CRITICAL -- MAJOR SUBSEQUENT RESTATEMENT, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED. All figures above are from Union Bank PLC's OWN, CONTEMPORANEOUS FY2023 annual report (unionbank-annual-report-2023.txt), audited by M M Rahman & Co. (Mohammed Forkan Uddin FCA, Managing Partner), signed 25 April 2024, with a CLEAN, UNQUALIFIED opinion ('the accompanying financial statements... give a true and fair view') and no going-concern paragraph. All internal identities reconcile exactly on this basis: Total Liabilities (279,009,675,195) + Total Equity (16,337,889,333) = Total Assets (295,347,564,528); Tier1 (1,623.80cr) + Tier2 (539.80cr) = Total Regulatory Capital (2,163.60cr); classified investments 9,263,050,359 / gross investments 255,691,913,189 = 3.62% (matches reported). 

HOWEVER, Union Bank PLC's own FY2024 annual report (unionbank-annual-report-2024.txt, audited by Syful Shamsul Alam & Co., signed 13 November 2025, with a QUALIFIED opinion including extensive fraud/manipulation findings and a going-concern paragraph) presents a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT FY2023 position in its own comparative column: Total Equity BDT 11,884.45m (not 16,337.89m); Total Tier-1 Capital BDT -55,329.39m and Total Regulatory Capital BDT -49,931.39m (both NEGATIVE, not the positive 1,623.80cr/2,163.60cr shown above) after deducting a 'Shortfall in Provision Required against NPI' of BDT 67,157.66m from CET-1 capital; CRAR -18.81% (not +11.11%); Net Profit after Tax BDT -2,875.22m, i.e. a LOSS (not the +1,607.89m PROFIT shown above); and -- most strikingly -- Classified Investments of BDT 106,510.90m, i.e. 41.66% of gross investments (not 9,263.05m / 3.62%), an over 11-fold increase versus what was originally reported for the identical balance-sheet date. 

The FY2024 report's own Qualified Opinion explicitly states the basis for this divergence: 'System-generated reports on classified investments were found to be manipulated in breach of IT protocols, showing significant deviations from actual balances', and 'Profit Suspense amount of Tk. 1,920.88 crore and Compensation amount of Tk. 41.84 crore totaling 1,962.72 crore was inappropriately recognized as Income which subsequently been reversed, as mentioned Bangladesh Bank Letter no. DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347 dated 29 April 2025' -- i.e. Bangladesh Bank's own investigation, conducted AFTER the original FY2023 audit was signed, found that the FY2023 (and presumably prior) classified-investment reporting had been manipulated and income had been improperly recognised. This is independently corroborated by contemporaneous Bangladesh press coverage found via web research: The Business Standard ('Union Bank's unholy union sank it in deep crisis') and a Union Bank Wikipedia summary both report that 'the 2023 revised financial report exposed... the bank shifted from a reported 1.62 billion taka profit to a 2.92 billion taka loss' -- matching this finding almost exactly (small rounding vs. the precise 1,607.89m / -2,875.22m figures above). 

Per this dataset's standing methodology ('prefer contemporaneous figures over later restated comparatives... record the divergence verbatim, never silently reconcile or average'), and because the FY2023 report is NOT internally arithmetically impossible (it reconciles perfectly on its own terms -- the problem is that its own UNDERLYING classification/income-recognition data was, per the successor auditor and Bangladesh Bank, later found to have been manipulated), this dataset's stored FY2023 values are the ORIGINAL figures, not the restated ones. This preserves consistency with how the rest of this dataset treats every other bank's FY2023 vs FY2024 (the sector-wide asset-quality shock is recorded as a FY2024 event); using Union Bank's restated, already-known-catastrophic FY2023 figures instead would make this one bank's FY2023 row incomparable with the other 35 banks' FY2023 rows. The restated figures are fully recorded here and in sources.json/insights.json so no information is lost. roa_pct/ldr_pct/cost_of_fund_pct/nav_per_share above are this report's own reported values (unaffected precision-wise by the restatement question, but see the same caveat: they are computed by the bank from the same now-disputed FY2023 book).

risk_signals.statement: Union Bank's FY2023 annual report was audited under a CLEAN, UNQUALIFIED opinion (M M Rahman & Co., signed 25 April 2024), reporting Shareholders' Equity of BDT 16,337.89m, CRAR of 11.11%, classified investments of BDT 9,263.05m (3.62% of gross investments), and Net Profit after Tax of BDT 1,607.89m. Union Bank's own FY2024 annual report -- audited a year later by a different firm (Syful Shamsul Alam & Co.) under a QUALIFIED opinion -- restates the identical FY2023 balance-sheet date to Shareholders' Equity BDT 11,884.45m, CRAR -18.81%, classified investments BDT 106,510.90m (41.66% of gross investments, an over 11-fold increase), and a NET LOSS of BDT -2,875.22m. The FY2024 report's own Qualified Opinion attributes this to 'System-generated reports on classified investments... manipulated in breach of IT protocols' and BDT 1,962.72 crore of income 'inappropriately recognized... which subsequently been reversed' per Bangladesh Bank letter DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347 (29 April 2025). This dataset stores the original, contemporaneous FY2023 figures per project methodology (see 2023_Q4.json's period_note and sources.json for the full restatement finding and independent press corroboration).

FY2024 net loss was BDT -257,936.69m -- independently corroborated by Bangladesh press (The Daily Star) reporting a 'Tk 25,790cr' loss, described as 'the biggest loss in [Bangladesh] banking history'. Shareholders' Equity swung from +BDT 16,337.89m (FY2023, originally reported) to -BDT 246,052.24m (FY2024) -- a single-year negative swing of over BDT 262 billion (262,390.13m), or about 16x the bank's entire FY2023 capital base. Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) fell to -405.31% (Total Regulatory Capital BDT -244,147.33m against Total Risk-Weighted Assets of BDT 60,237.66m), by far the most extreme CRAR reading in this dataset. Classified investments reached BDT 269,702.99m, i.e. 95.34% of gross investments of BDT 282,874.56m -- meaning fewer than 1 in 20 Taka of the bank's investment book was performing at year-end.

Newly-sourced Q1-Q3 2024 unaudited interim filings (added 2026-08-27) show Union Bank was still solvent and only mildly stressed as of 30 September 2024: Total Shareholders' Equity was BDT +15,964.45m (positive), 9-month cumulative Net Profit after Tax was BDT +147.66m (positive, though down sharply from BDT +949.47m at the June-2024 half-year point because of a discrete Q3-2024-alone LOSS of BDT -801.81m -- the first negative quarter in this bank's entire recorded interim series), and 9-month cumulative Total Provisions were BDT 1,550.50m (of which BDT 1,040.0m was booked in Q3 alone, roughly 4x the prior quarter and 9-14x every earlier quarter in the series). Combining these interim figures with this dataset's existing FY2024 annual figures (2024_Q4.json) shows the entire remainder of the year's damage landed in a single quarter: Q4-2024-ALONE net loss = -257,936.69m (FY total) minus +147.66m (9-month cumulative) = approximately -258,084.35m; Q4-2024-ALONE Total Provisions = 238,884.46m (FY total) minus 1,550.50m (9-month cumulative) = approximately 237,333.96m, i.e. about 153 times the combined first nine months; Q4-2024-ALONE equity swing = -246,052.24m (FY-end) minus +15,964.45m (30-Sept-2024) = approximately -262,016.69m. In other words, over 99.9% of the largest single-bank annual loss in Bangladeshi banking history was recognised in one unaudited-to-audited transition at year-end, not progressively through the year's own quarterly disclosures -- the interim filings gave real but comparatively modest warning (a single quarter's ~800m loss against a ~16 billion capital base) before the ~262 billion wipeout was booked.

Every one of Union Bank's own 2024 Q1, Q2 and Q3 unaudited interim filings (dated 25 April 2024, 30 July 2024 and 31 October 2024 respectively) reproduces its 'December 2023' comparative balance sheet column EXACTLY matching this dataset's stored ORIGINAL/contemporaneous FY2023 figures (Total Assets 295,347,564,528; Total Liabilities 279,009,675,195; Total Shareholders' Equity 16,337,889,333) -- NOT the figures Union Bank's own FY2024 annual report would later restate them to (Total Equity 11,884.45m, a loss of -2,875.22m instead of the originally-reported +1,607.89m profit). This is direct, dated proof that the classified-investment-data manipulation Bangladesh Bank found (letter DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347, dated 29 April 2025) had not yet been detected or reflected anywhere in Union Bank's own published numbers as late as 31 October 2024 -- over 22 months after the FY2023 year-end it concerns, and only about 6 months before the finding was made. Separately, every one of Union Bank's 2023 Q1/Q2/Q3 interim filings itself shows a smoothly IMPROVING trajectory throughout the year (cumulative Net Profit after Tax growing 353.90m to 839.47m to 1,367.50m; equity growing 15,627.12m to 15,584.84m to 16,102.31m) with no visible sign of trouble, consistent with the FY2023 annual report's own clean, unqualified audit opinion (M M Rahman & Co., signed 25 April 2024). This dataset's Q1-Q3 backfill therefore cannot identify any point at which the manipulation became visible in Union Bank's own published interim numbers before the FY2024 annual audit itself -- only that it was not visible in nine consecutive quarterly filings spanning January 2023 through September 2024.

The preceding finding was independently re-derived in a follow-up session (2026-08-28) by reading the raw OCR'd text of all three 2024 interim filings directly (annual_reports/UNIONBANK/unionbank-unaudited-2024-q1.txt, -q2.txt, -q3.txt), rather than relying on the prior session's summary. Each filing's own 'December 2023' comparative column, read verbatim, is IDENTICAL across all three and matches this dataset's stored ORIGINAL FY2023 values exactly -- Total Assets 295,347,564,528 and Total Shareholders' Equity 16,337,889,333 -- in the Q1 filing (as at 31 March 2024, signed 25 April 2024), the Q2 filing (as at 30 June 2024, signed 30 July 2024), and the Q3 filing (as at 30 September 2024, signed 31 October 2024) alike; none show the later-restated figures (equity 11,884.45m). This confirms, directly from primary-source line items rather than a derived summary, that Union Bank's own published books had genuinely not been restated as late as 31 October 2024, the latest-dated of the three filings and six months before Bangladesh Bank's manipulated-data finding letter (29 April 2025).

Union Bank's FY2024 Qualified Audit Opinion discloses that 74.20% of the bank's total Investment portfolio (BDT 20,989.72 crore / BDT 209,897.2m) was concentrated in a single borrower group, confirmed by Bangladesh Bank at a triparty meeting dated 23 April 2025 -- breaching the 15%-of-capital regulatory concentration ceiling under Section 26(B) of the Bank Company Act 1991 (as amended 2023) by a factor of roughly 5x. The auditor's report states this group meets the IAS 24 definition of a related party, yet Note 43 'Related Party Transactions' stated the Bank had no related-party transactions during the year -- a disclosure gap the auditors flagged directly. This concentration pattern is consistent with the broader S. Alam Group-linked bank resolution program documented elsewhere in this dataset (EXIMBANK's own FY2024 report explicitly names 'S Alam Group' related-party lending concentrations as its precipitating issue; this dataset's cross-bank research memo describes the five-bank Sammilito Islami Bank merger as resolving 'S Alam Group-linked banks' generally), though Union Bank's own FY2024 report does not itself name the group, and SIBL had not yet been examined in this dataset as of this writing.

Union Bank's Investment Deposit Ratio (IDR) exceeded 99% from FY2022 onward and breached 100% in FY2023 -- 99.64% (FY2022) and 108.50% (FY2023, originally reported, i.e. under the still-clean audit opinion) -- already far above the 92% regulatory ceiling that the FY2024 Qualified Audit Opinion later cites explicitly (IDR 115.63% in FY2024 'exceeding the regulatory ceiling of 92% prescribed by DOS Circular No. 02 dated 12 April 2020'). This means the liquidity-stress warning sign was visible in Union Bank's own published, audited numbers at least one full year (FY2023) before the auditors' qualification made it explicit -- IDR moved through 88.34% (FY2017), 96.03% (FY2018), 92.48% (FY2019), 90.22% (FY2020) and 91.55% (FY2021) before climbing to 99.64% (FY2022) and 108.50% (FY2023).

Classified investments as a percentage of gross investments rose steadily and continuously from 0.07% (FY2016) to 0.57% (FY2017) to 0.97% (FY2018) to 3.64% (FY2019) -- a greater-than-50x increase in three years, albeit from a very low base -- before plateauing in a 2.53%-3.62% band from FY2020 through FY2023 (originally reported). This multi-year, unbroken upward trend from a near-zero starting point through FY2019 was an early, visible signal of underwriting/asset-quality weakness years before the FY2024 collapse, even though the absolute levels through FY2023 (as originally reported) remained low by sector standards.

Union Bank's Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) started very high in its founding year (34.46% in FY2013, reflecting a small, newly-capitalized balance sheet) and declined steadily as the balance sheet scaled: 14.31% (FY2014), 13.27% (FY2015), 11.62% (FY2016), settling in an 10.24%-12.24% band from FY2017 through FY2023 (originally reported) -- consistently above the 10%-of-RWA minimum disclosed in the bank's own capital-adequacy notes throughout, but with little buffer above it in most years, leaving limited room to absorb the shock that materialized in FY2024.

Union Bank's FY2024 Balance Sheet is signed by a 'Deputy Managing Director', an 'Associate of Administrator' and an 'Administrator' -- rather than the Managing Director/Directors/Chairman panel that signed every prior year's balance sheet (FY2013-2023) -- confirming Bangladesh Bank had already placed the bank under administration before the FY2024 audit (signed 13 November 2025, ~10.5 months after fiscal year-end) was completed. The same report's going-concern paragraph discloses that 'on October 9, 2025, the Advisory Council of the Interim Government of Bangladesh approved the merger of this bank with other four banks... to form a new state-owned Islamic bank' -- i.e. the resolution process was already underway before the FY2024 annual report itself was finalized.

Union Bank never published a standalone FY2025 annual report and is very unlikely ever to. It was one of five distressed Shariah-based banks (with EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank) merged by Bangladesh Bank into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, as part of the resolution of S. Alam Group-linked banks. Bangladesh Bank declared Union Bank 'non-viable' under Section 15 of the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025, effective 5 November 2025 (the same date DSE suspended trading in its shares), and per independent press reporting shareholders of all five banks will receive no shares in the merged entity because the value of assets tied to their existing shareholding is already negative -- consistent with this dataset's own finding of BDT -246,052.24m shareholders' equity at FY2024 year-end. This is very likely a permanent series-end for Union Bank as a standalone reporting entity: any future consolidated figures for this business would appear, if at all, under Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, a distinct legal entity outside this dataset's scope.

insights.historical_context: Union Bank PLC is one of Bangladesh's youngest listed banks: incorporated 07 March 2013 as a Shariah-based Islamic bank from day one (unlike GIB, which converted from conventional banking mid-series), it grew its balance sheet from BDT 17,081.14m (partial-year FY2013) to BDT 295,347.56m (FY2023) over a decade -- a roughly 17-fold increase -- funded by rapid deposit growth (BDT 12,165.20m to BDT 225,585.37m) and completing an IPO/DSE listing in January 2022 that raised paid-up capital by about 77% (BDT 5,589.34m to BDT 9,869.34m). Profitability was consistently positive throughout FY2013-2023 (originally reported), with ROE (period-end equity basis) ranging from a first-year 1.94% up to a peak of 14.13% (FY2016) and settling in a 7.03%-10.80% band from FY2019-2023, and CRAR remaining above the bank's own 10%-of-RWA disclosed minimum throughout, albeit on a generally declining trend from a founding-year high of 34.46%. Classified investments crept up from a near-zero base (0.07% in FY2016) to 3.64% by FY2019, then plateaued in a 2.5%-3.6% band through FY2023 as originally reported -- a slow-burning asset-quality signal that, together with an Investment-Deposit Ratio that climbed past 99% (FY2022) and then 108% (FY2023), pointed toward mounting balance-sheet stress even under a still-clean audit opinion. The full scale of that stress was revealed only retrospectively: Union Bank's own FY2024 annual report shows its FY2023 comparative figures were built on 'manipulated' classified-investment system reports and improperly recognized income (per a Bangladesh Bank finding dated 29 April 2025), restating FY2023 from a BDT 1,607.89m profit and 11.11% CRAR to a BDT -2,875.22m loss and -18.81% CRAR. FY2024 itself was a full-blown collapse: a BDT -257,936.69m net loss (independently reported by Bangladesh media as the largest annual loss in the country's banking history), shareholders' equity of BDT -246,052.24m, CRAR of -405.31%, classified investments of 95.34% of gross investments, and a Qualified Audit Opinion documenting a 74.20%-of-portfolio single-borrower concentration, branch-level fraud findings, breached liquidity and capital-adequacy ratios, and a going-concern paragraph disclosing that Bangladesh Bank had already approved (9 October 2025) a merger of Union Bank with four other distressed Shariah-based banks -- EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank -- into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC. Bangladesh Bank formally declared Union Bank 'non-viable' effective 5 November 2025 and DSE suspended its share trading the same date; this dataset's Union Bank series therefore most likely ends at FY2024, with FY2024 standing as the bank's terminal standalone financial statement, and its equity holders receiving nothing in the resolution.
insights.data_gaps: Q4/year-end (audited) data spans FY2013 (partial, ~10-month first period) through FY2024. Q1/Q2/Q3 unaudited interim data (added 2026-08-27) is available for FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024 (9 quarters total) -- sourced from the bank's own 'Quarterly Statement' investor-relations page, which itself has no filing earlier than Q1 2022; a broad Wayback CDX sweep found no evidence any FY2013-2021 interim filing was ever published, plausibly because Union Bank only began publishing quarterly statements publicly around its January-2022 DSE listing (see sources.json) -- FY2013-2021 Q1-Q3 is therefore treated as a likely-genuine non-existence, not backfilled. Every 2022-2024 interim filing's balance-sheet identity and full P&L chain (Operating Income - Expenses = Operating Profit; - Provisions = PBT; - Tax = PAT) reconciles exactly to the Taka; small (<0.02 BDT-million, i.e. <0.002%) rounding-only differences appear when re-summing the *rounded* (2-decimal, BDT-million) figures stored in quarterly/*.json, an artifact of rounding several independently-derived line items rather than a data error -- the underlying raw-Taka source figures were verified with zero tolerance before rounding. Two of the nine interim filings (2022 Q1, 2023 Q1) were genuine text-layer PDFs extracted with pdftotext; the other seven were scanned-image PDFs independently OCR'd (pdftoppm + tesseract), cross-validated by the arithmetic reconciliation above and, where available, by an adjacent quarter's own reproduced comparative column. None of the nine interim filings disclose classified investments, NPL ratio, or CRAR/capital-adequacy figures -- these remain Q4/annual-only for this bank, unlike the flow figures (profit, provisioning) which are now visible quarterly for 2022-2024. FY2025 does not exist and is very unlikely to ever be published for Union Bank as a standalone entity -- confirmed via a time-boxed, multi-source check on 2026-08-26 (a Wayback CDX pass over the bank's own website found no FY2025-named filing and exposed a stale, misleadingly generic 'latest annual report' link that actually still points to the FY2021 report; the bank's own FY2024 report discloses the merger approval directly; and independent press confirms the non-viable declaration, trading suspension, and merger into Sammilito Islami Bank PLC) -- see sources.json and the merger_into_sammilito_islami_bank_series_end risk signal for the full finding. Several years' decorative 'Financial Performance at a Glance' / 'Annexure B Financial Highlights' summary pages (FY2013, FY2014, FY2015, FY2016, and FY2024) extracted as badly garbled or entirely blank text in this archive despite the surrounding core financial statements (Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, capital-adequacy notes) extracting cleanly; for those years, every figure in this dataset was instead sourced directly from the clean core statements and independently cross-checked against an adjacent year's comparative column (see each year's period_note and sources.json for the specific reconciliation). ldr_pct is available for every year FY2013-2023 (not FY2024, whose Annexure B was unreadable -- though the auditor's report separately quotes FY2024's IDR at 115.63%, recorded in 2024_Q4.json's period_note but not as a structured field since it was not independently cross-checked). roa_pct is available for FY2013 and FY2015-2023 but not FY2014 (the one year whose own summary page was both garbled AND not independently reproduced in an adjacent report's comparative column). cost_of_fund_pct is available only for FY2017-2023 (not FY2013-2016, whose own summary pages did not yield this field even after cross-referencing adjacent reports). nav_per_share is available only for FY2023 (reported) and FY2024 (calculated as total_equity/shares outstanding, since equity is negative that year) -- not a uniform gap but a reflection of which fields each year's own summary tables actually disclosed and which of those pages extracted legibly. A small number of cross-report figure discrepancies in the low single-digit-percent-or-smaller range were found and are documented in each affected year's period_note and in sources.json rather than silently reconciled (FY2015 total assets/liabilities ~0.018%, FY2018 Investment Deposit Ratio ~3.07pp / provision-kept ~0.86%, FY2019 total assets/liabilities ~0.046% and cost-of-fund ~3pp, FY2016 capital-adequacy presentation ~0.34%/0.04pp, FY2021 total assets/liabilities ~2.4%) -- all far smaller in both scale and consequence than the FY2023 restatement, which is the dataset's central finding for this bank. A follow-up session (2026-08-28) independently re-confirmed the FY2013-2021 Q1-Q3 non-existence via a full-domain (not keyword-filtered) Wayback CDX sweep of unionbank.com.bd covering all 3,630 of the domain's captures and manually reviewing every pre-2022-listing PDF found -- see sources.json for the detailed method and the newly-checked /psinformation/ disclosure-notice folder (itself only starting 2022-08-17, further corroborating the no-obligation-before-listing explanation). That session also independently re-verified, by reading the raw OCR'd source text of the 2024 Q1/Q2/Q3 filings directly rather than trusting the prior summary, that every one of their 'December 2023' comparative columns matches this dataset's stored original FY2023 figures exactly (see the corresponding risk_signal above). No new quarters were added; the 9-quarter (2022-2024) Q1-Q3 series remains this bank's ceiling absent a structural change (e.g. discovery of a pre-2022 private-placement disclosure), which this session judged unlikely enough not to be worth further chasing given the bank's series-end status.

sources.reporting_basis: SOLO / STANDALONE. Determined 2026-08-26. Union Bank PLC has no subsidiary. The FY2023 annual report's Basel-III capital-adequacy disclosures (Section B/C, 'Quantitative Disclosure: as on 31.12.2023') present the required 'Solo' and 'Consolidated' columns side by side for every capital-adequacy line item (CET-1, Tier-1, Tier-2, RWA, CRAR, etc.); the 'Consolidated' column is blank/dash ('-') throughout, and the qualitative narrative states explicitly: 'Union Bank PLC. is maintaining Capital to Risk Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) at 11.11% on SOLO basis against the regulatory minimum level of 12.50%.' Every Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss Account across all 12 archived years (2013-2024) is headed simply 'Balance Sheet' / 'Profit and Loss Statement' with no 'Consolidated' qualifier, i.e. Solo is the bank's only reporting basis, not one of two.
sources.notes: annual_reports/UNIONBANK archive covers 2013-2024 (12 text files, all sanity-checked as substantive, non-scanned extractions covering the full financial statements -- ranging 3,525 to 12,146 lines each). Union Bank PLC is a Shariah-based Islamic bank from inception (incorporated 07 March 2013): reports 'Investments' rather than conventional 'Loans and Advances', and 'Classified Investments' rather than 'NPL', consistent with EXIMBANK/FIRSTSBANK/GIB conventions already established in this dataset. The bank's own 'Financial Performance at a Glance' / 'Annexure B Financial Highlights' pages are ONLY ever a 2-year (current + prior) comparative in every report (never a genuine 5-year table despite the page sometimes being titled similarly to other banks' 5-year tables) -- so this dataset's full 12-year series was built by combining EVERY report's own 2-year window with its neighbours' overlapping comparative columns, cross-validating each figure at least twice. Two reports' decorative/highlights pages (FY2013's 'Financial Performance at a Glance'/'Details of Capital Fund', FY2015's same, and FY2016's and FY2013/2014's 'Annexure B Financial Highlights') extracted as badly garbled or entirely blank text in this archive despite the surrounding financial statements (Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Notes) extracting cleanly; for those years, figures were instead reconstructed directly from the clean Balance Sheet / Profit and Loss Account / Note 12.4 Capital Adequacy schedules, with row/label misalignment (FY2015) resolved by matching each row's prior-year comparative value against the adjacent report's own confirmed figures. FY2024's 'Annexure B Financial Highlights' page suffered the same OCR/extraction failure (numbers and labels fused/unreadable) -- the same category of fault documented for FIRSTSBANK's FY2024 report by a concurrent session -- and was not used for any figure; FY2024's figures come entirely from its own (cleanly-extracted) Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Statement and Note 12.4. Every 'basis':'reported' figure in this dataset was cross-checked against at least one other report's comparative column (see each year's period_note for the specific match/divergence found). CRITICAL FINDING: Union Bank's FY2023 annual report was audited by M M Rahman & Co. and gave a CLEAN, UNQUALIFIED opinion, but Union Bank's FY2024 annual report -- audited a year later by a different firm (Syful Shamsul Alam & Co.), which gave a QUALIFIED opinion citing manipulated classified-investment system reports and improperly recognised income (per Bangladesh Bank letter DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347 dated 29 April 2025) -- shows a completely different FY2023 position in its own comparative column (equity BDT 11,884.45m not 16,337.89m; CRAR -18.81% not +11.11%; a BDT -2,875.22m loss not a BDT +1,607.89m profit; classified investments BDT 106,510.90m / 41.66% of gross investments, not BDT 9,263.05m / 3.62%). Per this dataset's standing methodology, the ORIGINAL/contemporaneous FY2023 figures are stored as the dataset's FY2023 values (the report is not internally arithmetically impossible, it was the underlying data that was later found to have been manipulated) -- see the 2023 entry below and 2023_Q4.json's period_note for the full finding, independently corroborated by contemporaneous Bangladesh press coverage (The Business Standard, The Daily Star) found via web research. FY2024 is a catastrophic terminal year: net loss BDT -257,936.69m (independently corroborated by The Daily Star's reported 'Tk 25,790cr', the largest annual loss in Bangladeshi banking history), shareholders' equity BDT -246,052.24m, CRAR -405.31%, classified investments 95.34% of gross investments, and a 74.20%-of-portfolio single-borrower-group concentration flagged in the Qualified Audit Opinion. Union Bank was declared 'non-viable' by Bangladesh Bank effective 5 November 2025 (Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025, Section 15), DSE trading was suspended the same date, and the bank was merged -- together with EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank -- into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, under the same Bangladesh Bank resolution program documented independently by the concurrent sessions working EXIMBANK, GIB and FIRSTSBANK in this dataset; no standalone FY2025 report exists or is expected (see the FY2025 entry below). Only Q4/year-end (audited) data was extracted for any year; Q1/H1/Q3 unaudited interim data was not researched.

This report's own FY2023 comparative column, audited a year later (13 November 2025) by a DIFFERENT firm (Syful Shamsul Alam & Co.) under a QUALIFIED opinion, shows: Total Equity BDT 11,884.45m (vs BDT 16,337.89m originally reported); Total Tier-1 Capital BDT -55,329.39m and Total Regulatory Capital BDT -49,931.39m (both NEGATIVE, vs +BDT 1,623.80cr/+2,163.60cr originally) after deducting a 'Shortfall in Provision Required against NPI' of BDT 67,157.66m from CET-1; CRAR -18.81% (vs +11.11% originally); Net Profit after Tax BDT -2,875.22m, i.e. a LOSS (vs +BDT 1,607.89m PROFIT originally); and Classified Investments BDT 106,510.90m / 41.66% of gross investments (vs BDT 9,263.05m / 3.62% originally) -- an over 11-fold increase for the identical balance-sheet date. The FY2024 report's own Qualified Opinion states the basis explicitly: 'System-generated reports on classified investments were found to be manipulated in breach of IT protocols, showing significant deviations from actual balances', and that Profit Suspense (BDT 1,920.88 crore) and Compensation (BDT 41.84 crore) totalling BDT 1,962.72 crore 'was inappropriately recognized as Income which subsequently been reversed, as mentioned Bangladesh Bank Letter no. DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347 dated 29 April 2025'. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED via web research (2026-08-26): The Business Standard ('Union Bank's unholy union sank it in deep crisis') and a Union Bank Wikipedia summary both report that 'the 2023 revised financial report exposed... the bank shifted from a reported 1.62 billion taka profit to a 2.92 billion taka loss', closely matching (small rounding) this dataset's precise figures. Per this dataset's standing rule ('prefer contemporaneous figures over later restated comparatives... the one exception [is] if the contemporaneous figure is arithmetically impossible' -- FY2023's own report is NOT internally arithmetically impossible, it reconciles perfectly on its own terms), this dataset's stored FY2023 values are the ORIGINAL figures; this restated set is preserved here, in 2023_Q4.json's period_note, and in insights.json so no information is lost.

For the year ended 31 December 2024'; own Balance Sheet p.594-640; Profit and Loss Statement p.686-733; Note 12.4 Regulatory Capital Requirement p.2818-2846; Movement of classified Investments p.2176-2190; Notes 19-23 p.2890-2968)

Emran Hoshen, ACA, Partner), signed 13 November 2025 (~10.5 months after fiscal year-end) -- a QUALIFIED opinion with extensive fraud/going-concern findings (see 2024_Q4.json's period_note for the full list). This report's own 'Annexure B Financial Highlights' page extracted as badly OCR-garbled/scanned text (numbers and labels fused/unreadable) despite the surrounding Balance Sheet/P&L/Notes extracting cleanly -- the same category of fault documented for FIRSTSBANK's FY2024 report by a concurrent session; NOT used for any figure. The raw pdftotext output also lost the parenthesis/negative sign on several P&L rows (Net Investment Income, Profit/(Loss) before Provision and Tax, Deferred Tax); every such figure was independently re-derived from Note 19 (Investments income, 29 line items summed exactly to BDT 5,285,789,385) minus Note 20 (Profit Paid on Deposits, summed to BDT 21,184,832,524), cross-validating exactly against the reported Total Operating Income. All identities reconcile to the Taka: balance-sheet identity; Tier1+Tier2=Total Regulatory Capital; CRAR=Total Regulatory Capital/RWA=-405.31% exactly as the report itself states; PBT-Tax=PAT; classified investments/gross investments=95.34%. Balance sheet signed by 'Deputy Managing Director / Associate of Administrator / Administrator' (not the usual Managing Director/Directors/Chairman panel), confirming Bangladesh Bank had already placed the bank under administration by the signing date.

sources.notes: No FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025) annual report or audited financial statement exists for Union Bank PLC as a standalone entity, and this is very likely a PERMANENT series-end, not a routine reporting lag. This dataset's FY2024 report (unionbank-annual-report-2024.txt, signed 13 November 2025) already discloses, in its own going-concern paragraph, that 'on October 9, 2025, the Advisory Council of the Interim Government of Bangladesh approved the merger of this bank with other four banks, under the direction of Bangladesh Bank, to form a new state-owned Islamic bank' -- i.e. the merger was approved before FY2025 (Jan-Dec 2025) had even closed, and the FY2024 report itself was signed under active administration (see the 2024 entry above). Independently confirmed via a time-boxed check on 2026-08-26, per this dataset's standing approach for banks in this same resolution program (see FIRSTSBANK, GIB): (1) a Wayback Machine CDX API pass over unionbank.com.bd's reports paths found the bank's site has PDFs only through 'financial-statement-24.pdf' (the FY2024 statement, crawled 2025-12-27, matching the FY2024 report already in this archive) and a generic, persistently-named 'ubl-annual-report.pdf' whose crawled content (checked directly, downloaded and inspected via pdfinfo/pdftotext, then deleted per project policy) turned out to be a stale, unrefreshed copy of the FY2021 annual report (Adobe InDesign creation date June 2022) rather than a new FY2025 filing -- no FY2025-named file exists in the CDX index at all; (2) a live fetch of unionbank.com.bd shows the site still branded 'Union Bank PLC' with normal-looking recent activity (a '185th board meeting, November 2025') but ALSO shows its logo linking to 'sammilitobankbd.com' and some internal URLs/page titles already referencing 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC', i.e. the merger is already bleeding into the live site; (3) an attempted DSE (dsebd.org) company-page fetch was inconclusive (certificate/dynamic-content issues meant only a stale-looking 'Last AGM held on: 15-06-2023' was retrievable, itself consistent with a disrupted AGM cycle but not independently conclusive); (4) general web/news search independently and strongly corroborates the merger: Bangladesh Bank declared Union Bank 'non-viable' under Section 15 of the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025 effective 5 November 2025 and DSE suspended its share trading the same date (The Business Standard, 'Share trading of 5 troubled Islamic banks suspended before merger'), alongside EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank; shareholders of all five banks will receive no shares in the merged entity because 'the value of assets tied to their existing shareholding is already negative' (The Daily Star); Union Bank entered the merger with (per a KPMG review) an NPL ratio of 97.8% as of September 2024 and a record FY2024 loss of 'Tk 25,790cr... the biggest loss in [Bangladesh] banking history' (The Daily Star) -- matching this dataset's own FY2024 figures closely; the five banks were merged into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC (Bangladesh Bank Letter of Intent issued 9 November 2025; a final operating licence reported granted in late 2025; Sammilito began a phased rollout of operations starting 2 December 2025 per some contemporaneous reports, with fuller integration by 18 August 2026 per this dataset's cross-bank research on the sibling banks EXIMBANK/GIB/FIRSTSBANK -- sources found in this session's research were not fully consistent on the exact 'independent operations' date, and this is recorded rather than adjudicated). Because the resolution/merger process was already underway before FY2025 even closed, and the bank was already operating under a Bangladesh-Bank-appointed Administrator by the time its (delayed, ~10.5-months-late) FY2024 report was even signed, there is no realistic expectation that a standalone FY2025 'Union Bank PLC' annual report will ever be filed; any FY2025-and-later reporting for this banking business would presumably surface, if at all, under 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC' -- a distinct legal entity outside this dataset's scope. No 2025_Q4.json file was created for this bank.

sources.source_document: unionbank.com.bd's own 'Quarterly Statement' investor-relations page (https://unionbank.com.bd/quarterly-statement, a different page than /annual-reports), which lists 9 downloadable 'Condensed Balance Sheet' + 'Condensed Profit and Loss Account' un-audited interim PDFs spanning Q1 2022 through Q3 2024 -- the bank's live site was NOT disrupted despite its crisis/administration/merger status, and every filing downloaded directly from the live URLs shown below (cross-checked byte-for-byte against the largest available Wayback Machine capture of each; the live copies were consistently the largest/most complete)
sources.note: 9 files found and used, one per quarter: 2022 Q1 (https://unionbank.com.bd/assets/reports/half/Quarterly-Financial-Statement-as-on-31-March-2022.pdf), 2022 Q2/H1 (.../Half_Yearly_FS_2022_____.pdf), 2022 Q3 (.../Un-audited_Quarterly_Statement_Q3_as_on_30th_September,_2022.pdf), 2023 Q1 (.../1st-quarter-2023-ubl.pdf), 2023 Q2/H1 (.../2nd-q-ubl.pdf), 2023 Q3 (.../3rd_Quarter_Financial_Statement_as_on_30_September_2023.pdf), 2024 Q1 (.../31_March_2024.pdf), 2024 Q2/H1 (.../FS_30-06-2024.pdf), 2024 Q3 (.../Accounts.pdf, titled 'Quarterly Financial Statement as on 30 September 2024' on the listing page). 2022 Q1 and 2023 Q1 were genuine text-layer PDFs, extracted cleanly with pdftotext -layout. The other 7 were SCANNED IMAGE PDFs (2022 Q3 had zero usable embedded text; the other 6 had a badly corrupted/broken-font-encoding text layer that scrambled digits) -- all 7 were independently OCR'd (pdftoppm 300dpi + tesseract); every OCR'd figure's internal arithmetic (balance-sheet identity; Total Operating Income - Expenses = Operating Profit; - Provisions = PBT; - Tax = PAT) reconciles EXACTLY to the Taka for all 9 quarters, and every quarter's own prior-year comparative column was independently cross-checked against this dataset's corresponding quarter file where both exist (all matches, no discrepancies) -- strong corroboration that the OCR is reliable. A handful of individual P&L sub-lines ('Investments Income' gross and 'Profit Paid on Deposits', i.e. the pre-netting interest-income/interest-expense-equivalent figures) were illegible in specific quarters' own OCR; where recoverable, they were cross-referenced from an adjacent quarter's own comparative column (2022 Q2, 2023 Q3) or derived by subtraction from other confirmed figures (calculated_from_pl_components) -- flagged per-line-item in each quarterly/*.json file's basis field; never fabricated. PDFs deleted after extraction per project policy; the extracted/OCR'd text is retained at annual_reports/UNIONBANK/unionbank-unaudited-<year>-q<n>.txt for all 9 quarters. CRITICAL CROSS-VALIDATION FINDING (see insights.json for the full narrative): every 2024 Q1/Q2/Q3 filing's own 'December 2023' comparative column reproduces this dataset's stored ORIGINAL/contemporaneous FY2023 figures (Total Equity 16,337,889,333; Total Assets 295,347,564,528) EXACTLY, not the later-restated figures -- direct, dated proof that Union Bank's own books had not yet been restated as late as the Q3 2024 filing date (31 October 2024), six months before Bangladesh Bank's manipulated-data finding letter (29 April 2025). The Q1/Q2 2024 filings show continued normal, healthy, growing figures with no visible warning sign; Q3 2024 (30 September 2024) is the first quarter in the whole series to show a discrete quarterly LOSS (-801.81m), a quarter-on-quarter equity decline, and a sharp spike in classified-investment provisioning (1,040.0m for the quarter alone, vs a 100-460m range in every prior quarter) -- a real but comparatively modest crack, utterly dwarfed by the scale of what followed: combining this filing's 9-month cumulative figures with this dataset's existing 2024_Q4.json shows the IMPLIED Q4-2024-ALONE net loss was approximately -258,084.35m (BDT million) and Q4-2024-ALONE provisioning was approximately 237,333.96m (roughly 153x the entire first nine months combined) -- i.e. essentially the entire Bangladesh-record-setting FY2024 collapse was recognised in a single quarter (Q4, Oct-Dec 2024) at year-end audit, not gradually through the year's interim filings. None of the Q1-Q3 filings for any year (2022-2024) disclose classified investments, NPL ratio, or CRAR/capital-adequacy figures -- these condensed interim statements only cover the Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Cash Flow Statement, Statement of Changes in Equity, and a handful of selective notes (provisions-by-category, taxation, NAV/EPS); Basel-III capital disclosures appear only in the audited Annual Report.

sources.notes: The bank's own 'Quarterly Statement' page and a broad Wayback CDX sweep of unionbank.com.bd (all captures containing 'quarter'/'interim'/'half' in the URL, back to the domain's earliest crawl) turn up NO quarterly/interim financial-statement PDF earlier than 'Quarterly-Financial-Statement-as-on-31-March-2022.pdf' (first archived 2022-07-05); the 'quarterly-statement' listing page itself is first archived 2022-01-21 -- five days before Union Bank's DSE listing (26 January 2022). This is consistent with (not proof of, but a plausible explanation for) Union Bank only beginning to PUBLISH quarterly interim statements publicly around the time of its IPO/DSE listing, when BSEC's public periodic-disclosure requirements for listed companies would have first applied to it; before that it was privately held (still reporting to Bangladesh Bank, but with no obligation to publish quarterly statements for public/investor consumption). No FY2013-2021 Q1/Q2/Q3 files were found and none are claimed to exist -- this is recorded as a likely-genuine non-existence, not a research gap, consistent with this dataset's standing rule to never backfill or fabricate a quarter that cannot be genuinely sourced.

sources.period: 2013-2021 Q1/Q2/Q3 (unaudited interim) -- INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-28, still not found
sources.notes: A follow-up session re-checked this gap from scratch with a broader method than the prior sweep: pulled the Wayback CDX API for the ENTIRE unionbank.com.bd domain with no keyword filter (3,630 total captures) and manually reviewed every one of the 127 PDF captures timestamped before 2022-01-21 (five days before the bank's DSE listing). Every pre-listing PDF is either an annual document ('financial_statements_for_the_year_of_31_december_20XX.pdf' for 2013-2019, annual-report PDFs, or annual Basel-II/III risk-based-capital disclosure PDFs) or unrelated (branch openings, forms, career postings, CSR/PR notices) -- zero quarterly, half-yearly, or condensed interim statements of any kind appear anywhere in the domain's pre-2022 crawl, under any path, not just the /assets/reports/half/ and /quarterly-statement paths the prior session already checked. Also newly checked a /assets/reports/psinformation/ folder (DSE-mandated Price Sensitive Information / disclosure notices, several titled '...Quarterly_Un-Audited_FS...') that the prior sweep's keyword filter had missed: its own earliest Wayback capture of any file is 2022-08-17 ('PSI_and_Disclosure_of_Quarterly_Un-Audited_FS1.pdf') -- i.e. this disclosure channel itself only starts appearing about 7 months after the bank's January-2022 listing, further corroborating (not contradicting) the 'no public quarterly-disclosure obligation before listing' explanation already on record. Net result: this independently reconfirms, via a materially broader full-domain sweep, the prior session's conclusion -- 2013-2021 Q1/Q2/Q3 unaudited interim statements were very likely never published for public consumption. Structurally analogous to this dataset's NRBBANK finding (no BSEC obligation before its own IPO). Separately noted here for a FUTURE session, and explicitly NOT pursued in this one (out of scope -- this task was instructed not to chase FY2025 data given the Sammilito Islami Bank merger series-end): a Wayback capture (first seen 2025-07-23) of https://unionbank.com.bd/news/half-yearly-business-conference-2025-of-union-bank-plc shows the bank held a 'Half Yearly Business Conference 2025', implying a H1-2025 (Jan-Jun 2025) unaudited interim statement may have been prepared internally even after FY2024's catastrophic collapse and before the 9-Oct-2025 merger approval / 5-Nov-2025 non-viable declaration. This does not change this dataset's FY2024 series-end determination (equity was already -246,052.24m and the bank was already under Bangladesh Bank administration by the time the delayed FY2024 audit was signed), but is flagged in case a future session's scope ever extends to FY2025.

Q4.notes: Confirmed unavailable 2026-08-26: Union Bank was declared non-viable (Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025 Sec 15) effective 5-Nov-2025, trading suspended same day, merged into the newly formed state-owned Sammilito Islami Bank PLC together with EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, and Social Islami Bank under Bangladesh Bank resolution of S Alam Group-linked banks (Advisory Council approved the merger 9-Oct-2025, before FY2025 even closed). Permanent series-end, not a reporting lag. This is the 5th and final bank of that merger group now accounted for in this dataset.
